candidates.name: LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud
verified_facts: The Environment Agency point-cloud archive contains 3D x,y,z points and attributes; DTM and DSM time-stamped raster products are derived from point-cloud data.
Site-specific LIDAR surveys have been carried out across England since 1998; point-cloud holdings are available for surveys going back to 2006.
Ground and surface-object returns are classified, but manual editing of the derived DTM means classified ground points need not exactly match the final DTM.
semantic_limits: Point-cloud availability is not guaranteed for every historical surface model.
Point-cloud ground classifications are supporting lineage evidence, not a substitute for the final edited DTM parcel measurement.

candidates.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles
verified_facts: The archive provides DTM rasters at 25 cm, 50 cm, 1 m and 2 m depending on survey.
Data is in metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and aligned to the OS Grid.
The dataset states vertical accuracy of +/-15 cm RMSE and records survey-specific transformation/geoidal-model metadata.
semantic_limits: Survey-period transformation and geoid information must be preserved when historical tiles are compared with current composite results.
The +/-15 cm RMSE statement is a source-survey accuracy contract, not a parcel-specific confidence interval.

candidates.name: LIDAR DSM Time Stamped Tiles
verified_facts: The DSM archive includes terrain plus objects such as buildings, vehicles and vegetation.
Data is supplied in metres referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and aligned to the OS Grid.
The dataset states vertical accuracy of +/-15 cm RMSE.
semantic_limits: DSM values are not valid replacements for bare-earth DTM parcel-height results.
DSM is used only to detect or explain surface-object contamination and must remain separate from the DTM result.

candidates.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) 10m
verified_facts: The 10 m composite is an Environment Agency bare-earth DTM covering approximately 99% of England.
It is resampled from the LIDAR Composite DTM 2 m dataset using bilinear interpolation.
The composite combines time-stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
semantic_limits: At 10 m resolution this product is a coarse terrain sanity check only and cannot replace the 1 m primary parcel measurement.
Because it derives from the 2 m composite it is not an independent survey-error crosscheck.

candidates.name: OS Terrain 50 source data
verified_facts: OS Terrain source data models bare earth in a triangulated irregular network using mass points, breaklines and automated/photogrammetric techniques.
Grid and contour products are interpolated from the source TIN.
For mainland areas, terrain heights are generally relative to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
semantic_limits: OS Terrain 50 is generalised for small-scale use and remains a coarse sanity layer for parcel-scale work.
Its source-model semantics support interpretation but do not improve the measured EA 1 m parcel value by themselves.

candidates.name: Ordnance Datum Newlyn
verified_facts: ODN is the mainland Great Britain national height datum used by Ordnance Survey.
Ordnance Survey warns that legacy bench marks can suffer movement or subsidence and should not automatically be treated as high-precision current control.
OSGM15 relates ODN orthometric heights to GNSS ellipsoid heights.
semantic_limits: Legacy bench-mark observations are not used to overwrite the raster result without a dated survey and traceable transformation.
Datum-reference evidence is separate from terrain-sampling uncertainty.

candidates.name: Future of British mapping coordinate systems
verified_facts: OSGB36 and ODN remain the basis of OS mapping, with OS Net used to access them through transformations from ETRS89.
Ordnance Survey identifies OSTN15 and OSGM15 as the current horizontal and vertical transformation models for this workflow context.
semantic_limits: Transformation guidance establishes coordinate/datum handling but does not validate a parcel polygon or elevation sample by itself.
Transformation evidence must be joined to exact CRS, source raster and polygon evidence.

candidates.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons spatial data metadata
verified_facts: HM Land Registry is the publisher and the dataset is licensed under the Open Government Licence.
The metadata was updated on 8 July 2026.
The dataset contains locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales and is supplied by local-authority area.
semantic_limits: INSPIRE polygons show indicative extents and are not legal boundary determinations.
Current publication metadata does not by itself prove that a locally cached polygon file is the same current edition; file hashes remain required.
